chapterName: Early Rome & the Kingdom: The Foundation of an Empire (753-509 BCE)

questions.question: What did Brutus do when his own sons were caught plotting to bring Tarquin back?
options: Sent them into exile at Cumae
questions.explanation: Brutus ordered the execution of his own sons for plotting the king's return. He had made the people swear never again to accept a king.
questions.sourceQuote: When his own sons were caught plotting to bring Tarquin back, he ordered their execution.

questions.question: Which emperor identified Servius Tullius with Mastarna, an Etruscan adventurer who became king of Rome?
questions.explanation: The emperor Claudius made this identification in the first century AD. The historian Momigliano warned that Mastarna is so unlike the traditional Servius that the two are best kept apart.
questions.sourceQuote: The emperor Claudius, in the first century AD, identified Servius with Mastarna, an Etruscan adventurer who became king of Rome.

questions.question: After the Romans and Sabines united, which Sabine king shared the throne with Romulus?
questions.explanation: Once the two peoples united, the Sabine king Titus Tatius ruled jointly with Romulus. The union followed the war over the seized Sabine women.
questions.sourceQuote: The two peoples then united, and the Sabine king Titus Tatius shared the throne with Romulus.

questions.question: Later Romans traced the family of Romulus and Remus back to which hero, who fled the fall of Troy?
questions.explanation: Later Romans linked the twins' family to Aeneas, a refugee from fallen Troy. Most modern historians treat this whole founding story as myth.
questions.sourceQuote: Later Romans also traced the twins' family back to Aeneas, a hero who fled the fall of Troy.

questions.question: Which religious institutions is Numa Pompilius credited with creating? (select all that apply)
options: The Temple of Diana on the Aventine
questions.explanation: Numa founded the Vestal Virgins and created the office of chief priest. He was a Sabine chosen for his justice and piety.
questions.sourceQuote: He also founded the Vestal Virgins and created the office of chief priest.

questions.question: When a king died, what did the interrex, or "between-king", do?
options: Commanded the army until a new war began
Organised the dead king's funeral games
Guarded the royal treasury for the heir
Ruled for a full year until the Senate voted
Served five days to find a candidate for the throne
questions.explanation: A senator served as interrex for five days to find a candidate, then handed over to another senator if he failed. The chosen man was then presented to the Curiate Assembly.
questions.sourceQuote: One senator became the interrex, or "between-king", serving for five days to find a candidate, then handing over to another if he failed.

questions.question: How was the new voting assembly based on Servius Tullius's wealth classes organised?
options: So that plebeians outvoted the nobles
So that every citizen had an equal vote
So that each district voted equally
So that the rich had the most influence
So that only patricians could vote
questions.explanation: Servius's five wealth classes formed a voting assembly weighted towards the rich. Later, though, he was said to favour the poor at the nobles' expense.
questions.sourceQuote: These classes became the basis of a new voting assembly, organised so that the rich had the most influence.

questions.question: Lucretia's story closely resembles a Greek tale about which event?
options: The fall of the tyrants of Athens
questions.explanation: Lucretia's story mirrors a Greek tale about the fall of Athens' tyrants around 510 BC, which makes Rome's version suspect. Some historians think Rome's kingship faded slowly rather than ending in one dramatic night.
questions.sourceQuote: Lucretia's story closely resembles a Greek tale about the fall of the tyrants of Athens, around 510 BC.

questions.question: Tarquin the Proud was the son of which earlier king?
questions.explanation: Tarquin the Proud was the son of Tarquinius Priscus, while Servius Tullius was his father-in-law. According to tradition he ruled for 25 years.
questions.sourceQuote: He was the son of the earlier king Tarquinius Priscus, and according to tradition he ruled for 25 years.

questions.question: Tarquinius Priscus added 100 new members to the Senate. How large did that make it?
questions.explanation: The extra 100 members raised the Senate to 200. Tarquinius also reportedly doubled Rome's size through wars against the Sabines and Etruscans.
questions.sourceQuote: He added 100 new members to the Senate, raising it to 200.
